newsitem.title: UK: Dalgety shares drop after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Dalgety shares drop after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in foods-to-agribusiness group Dalgety Plc tumbled in pre-market trading on Tuesday after the company issued its second profit warning in two months.
The stock was down 40p, or 15 percent, at 221-1/2 by 0706 GMT in volume of 35,000 shares.
In a trading statement, Dalgety said its profits for the past year ended June 30 would be lower than expected because of poor fourth-quarter trading and higher one-off charges.

Chairman Denys Henderson said the results were "unacceptable" and shareholder value "must be restored". He said management action would produce benefits that would become apparent during fiscal 1998 and beyond.

The warning came after Dalgety shares tumbled on May 7 after the company said its second-half results would fall short of its performance in the first half of the year. It also said it would cut its dividend.
By 0712 GMT Dalgety shares had fallen 42-1/2p to 219 -- about half its year's high of 447p set on March 8.
